name: Erechtheion
subtitle: temple of Athena of the City

name: Acropolis
note: The high city. Every building up here has a glowing doorway: find them all.

name: Stoa of Eumenes
note: A stoa is a long covered walkway, for shade and gossip. The Stoics took their name from a different one, the Painted Stoa in the Agora. Zeno's flag is there, and Marcus Aurelius waits at the Tower of the Winds.

name: Stoa of Attalos
subtitle: shopping arcade, now a museum
note: A king of Pergamon gave Athens this shopping arcade. It was rebuilt in the 1950s, and today it is the Agora museum. Go and look at the voting machines.

name: Roman Agora
note: The Romans' market square. Look for the Gate of Athena, still standing. The Tower of the Winds is at the far end.

name: Hadrian's Arch
subtitle: the emperor's gate
note: Emperor Hadrian built this gate. One side says: This is Athens, the old city of Theseus. The other side says: This is the city of Hadrian, not of Theseus.

name: Acropolis Museum
subtitle: the treasures inside
note: The Acropolis Museum. The real Caryatids live inside, and the glass floor shows a Roman street underneath.

name: Philopappos Monument
subtitle: a prince's tomb
note: The tomb of a Roman prince who loved Athens. Best view of the Acropolis from up here.

name: Lysicrates Monument
note: A rich man won a prize for a play and built this little tower to show off his trophy.

name: Anafiotika
note: A tiny village of white houses built by islanders from Anafi, who came to build the king's palace.

name: Plaka
note: The oldest streets of modern Athens: shops, cats and tavernas.

name: Epicurus's Garden
note: Epicurus taught in a garden here. Happiness, he said, means friends, bread and no fear.

name: Kerameikos
note: The potters' quarter and the old cemetery, just outside the city wall.
